title: David Enoch vs Lance Bush: Are There Objective Moral Truths?
label: Moral realism and anti-realism
motion: Are there objective moral truths, and does moral realism or global normative anti-realism better explain ordinary moral judgment, deliberation, language, and disagreement?
sourceNote: Assessment based exclusively on the complete locally cached YouTube caption transcript and timestamped events (transcript SHA-256 a6db7b0ca58006c793bf1207c55a907c9a66e0692b3bd14d5b4a849f3be90aa0). Required below-high-confidence audio checks were completed before adjudication; representative quotations must be exact strings from quote-eligible locked source spans.
scoringNote: Scores are AI-generated estimates of argumentative performance under the locked adjudicated-consensus workflow. Repository code calculated every move, section, and overall result once, only after two isolated judgments, required audio review, and disputed-field adjudication closed.
summary: Enoch defends mind-independent normativity through justified appearances and comparative explanation; Bush contests realist priority through neutral language, causal genealogy, pragmatism, and parsimony.

pro.text: They do not depend constitutively on us in any way.
pro.context: Enoch uses this formulation to specify the mind-independence central to his robust non-naturalist account of objective normative truth.

con.text: I deny normative realism as a whole.
con.context: Bush clarifies that his opposition extends beyond morality to the entire normative domain, preserving the debate's fundamental disagreement.

pro.words: Morality belongs within the broader normative domain, which also contains epistemic and prudential truths that are not straightforwardly classified as moral.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The taxonomic clarification is unusually precise, illustrates broader normativity through epistemic justification, and efficiently prevents the discussion from becoming artificially restricted to conventionally moral propositions. Principal limitation: Establishing that morality is one normative subset does not itself establish that normative facts exist independently, deserve explanatory inclusion, or share identical metaphysical and epistemological credentials across domains. Live burden: The realist must connect this clarified scope to a warranted account of normative facts as data while addressing whether epistemic norms provide legitimate support rather than merely transferring the original controversy. Locked score: The very strong band reflects excellent coherence, stable terminology, explicit qualification, and central methodological relevance, tempered only by the clarification's necessarily incomplete contribution to the larger realist demonstration.

con.words: Global normative anti-realism denies realism throughout the normative domain, so broadening the subject beyond morality preserves fundamental disagreement while reducing the moral versus nonmoral boundary's centrality.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The reply accepts the realist's broader framing without evasion, precisely defines global normative anti-realism, and demonstrates that the expanded scope leaves direct opposition fully intact. Principal limitation: Because this is principally a clarification of Bush's own position, it does not yet provide affirmative considerations supporting global denial or explain whether distinct normative domains require differentiated treatment. Live burden: The anti-realist must develop a domain-spanning account capable of handling moral, epistemic, and prudential normativity while showing why similarities among them support rejection rather than realism. Locked score: The very strong band appropriately recognizes exceptional responsiveness, near-complete motion contact, stable scope, careful qualification, and charitable uptake of the opposing clarification, while acknowledging that positional precision cannot substitute for the later constructive defense.

pro.words: A satisfactory realism must address epistemic, semantic, motivational, and disagreement objections while comparatively testing whether rival theories preserve the relevant normative phenomena.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The move articulates a demanding, methodologically evenhanded research program that combines objection handling with holistic comparison rather than treating realist description as sufficient vindication. Principal limitation: A statement of appropriate evaluative burdens remains programmatic and cannot establish that realism actually satisfies them, especially where the relevant phenomena and comparative theoretical costs require independent specification. Live burden: The realist must operationalize preservation, explanatory adequacy, and theoretical expense, then represent serious rival packages concretely enough for cumulative comparison rather than relying upon generalized references to alternatives. Locked score: The very strong band recognizes exceptional coherence, responsiveness to the debate's central comparative structure, and accurately calibrated necessity, while withholding stronger commendation because the methodological framework anticipates rather than completes the required demonstration.

con.words: Realism gains no automatic holistic advantage when anti-realists challenge, rather than concede, alleged costs such as abandoning ordinary discourse or rejecting shared intuitions.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The reply correctly exposes that a holistic comparison cannot count controversial anti-realist concessions as settled costs, and it preserves the realist's comparative method while contesting its inputs. Principal limitation: Rejecting inherited cost assignments does not itself show that the disputed costs disappear, nor does the selected evidence provide a developed alternative accounting of semantic, epistemic, motivational, and ontological liabilities. Live burden: The anti-realist must demonstrate how ordinary discourse and intuitive practice remain available within a specified rival framework, then compare that framework's actual commitments against realism under shared criteria. Locked score: The very strong band reflects direct and charitable responsiveness, coherent burden contact, and appropriately qualified force, balanced by limited positive evidence for the proposed reassessment of comparative expenses.

pro.words: Inability to compel a radical dissenter does not defeat a highly plausible premise's justification or establish epistemic parity between opposed starting points.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The reply sharply distinguishes dialectical power from epistemic justification, thereby blocking the mistaken inference that an inability to force skeptical assent automatically defeats an otherwise warranted premise. Principal limitation: Answering defeat through disagreement does not establish the comparative warrant of the realist starting point, and the radical-skeptic analogy risks understating Bush's request for differentiating considerations. Live burden: The realist must provide positive grounds for ranking the competing appearances without requiring universal persuasion, while explaining why the anti-realist challenge resembles radical skepticism rather than reasonable peer disagreement. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptional directness, coherent reasoning, calibrated qualification, and strong central relevance, tempered by the remaining need to justify privilege instead of merely defending permissibility.

con.words: Ordinary discourse and deliberation need not embody implicit realism or anti-realism, and realist intuitions are neither universal nor entitled to automatic methodological priority.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The reply avoids manufacturing popular anti-realism, instead advancing the more careful conclusion that ordinary practice may remain neutral between substantive metaethical interpretations. Principal limitation: Its empirical generalization is only referenced rather than demonstrated, leaving insufficient representative evidence that ordinary speakers lack implicit realist commitments across the relevant judgments, contexts, and formulations. Live burden: The anti-realist must specify testable indicators distinguishing pragmatic objectivity from metaphysical commitment and show that neutral interpretations explain objective-seeming usage at least comparably well. Locked score: The very strong band recognizes strong logical discipline, explicit qualification, excellent contact with the realist's claimed explanandum, and charitable engagement with implicit commitment, while retaining a significant evidential reservation concerning the population-level attribution.

pro.words: Inquiry must begin from comparatively plausible appearances, and an opponent's persistent rejection cannot by itself threaten the position grounded upon the more plausible starting point.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The move offers a practical methodology for inquiry under foundational disagreement and explicitly acknowledges the possibility of unresolved epistemic impasse rather than promising compulsory persuasion. Principal limitation: Comparative plausibility remains unspecified and potentially participant-relative, so invoking it does not establish that realist appearances outrank anti-realist alternatives or avoid reproducing the original disagreement. Live burden: The realist must articulate publicly assessable considerations governing plausibility, distinguish prima facie justification from dialectical convenience, and demonstrate their application without assuming the realist conclusion. Locked score: The very strong band recognizes excellent responsiveness, stable scope, necessary methodological insight, and thoughtful qualification, while preserving material reservations about evidential warrant, operational criteria, and the uncompleted comparative case for privileging this particular starting point.

con.words: Realist appearances receive no privilege merely from intuitive force, because opposed starting assumptions face symmetrical circularity concerns and require further considerations to break the impasse.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The symmetry challenge directly identifies the unresolved epistemic question and carefully uses hallucination or colorblindness as possibilities undermining automatic privilege rather than as demonstrations of realist error. Principal limitation: Symmetrical dialectical starting points do not necessarily possess symmetrical justification, and the analogy supplies no independent reason for treating the realist appearance as unreliable or comparatively deficient. Live burden: The anti-realist must identify further considerations that distinguish disagreement from defeat, explain how comparative warrant should be assessed, and supply evidence favoring an error-producing mechanism or neutral methodology. Locked score: The very strong band reflects excellent responsiveness, explicit calibration, substantial charity, and central relevance, alongside appropriately significant reservations about evidential support and the inference from unshared intuition to epistemic parity.

pro.words: Robust non-naturalist realism treats objective normative truths as mind-independent, nonconventional facts whose recognition can vindicate ordinary normative judgment and deliberation.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The move precisely identifies robust realism's constitutive commitments, directly connects mind-independence with the motion, and establishes an exceptionally relevant foundation for the subsequent vindication project. Principal limitation: Its broader explanatory promise remains comparatively underdeveloped because describing objective truths does not independently demonstrate that positing them successfully vindicates ordinary judgment, deliberation, language, or motivation. Live burden: The realist must therefore supplement this metaphysical characterization with a discriminating account showing why objective facts explain those practices more comprehensively than sophisticated attitude-based, pragmatist, or expressivist alternatives. Locked score: The very strong band appropriately reflects outstanding motion relevance, clear recoverability, and disciplined terminology while preserving substantial reservation about evidential support for the announced explanatory conclusion.

con.words: Steadfast moral opposition and counterfactual standards do not entail realism, because anti-realism can distinguish first-order commitment from metaethical interpretation and accommodate objective-seeming responses.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The reply clearly separates unwavering first-order condemnation from second-order metaphysical commitment, preventing ordinary moral seriousness from being treated as a straightforward entailment of realism. Principal limitation: Demonstrating logical compatibility with anti-realism is weaker than providing an equally comprehensive explanation, and the positive account of actual versus counterfactual standards remains compressed in the selected evidence. Live burden: The anti-realist must supply semantics and pragmatics explaining stable counterfactual wrongness, sincere disagreement, and action guidance without covertly importing mind-independent truth conditions. Locked score: The very strong band reflects excellent direct responsiveness, stable distinctions, calibrated force, and meaningful support for the language-practice bridge, balanced by lower central burden completion and the continuing gap between accommodation and comparative explanatory success.

pro.words: Ordinary subjectivist paraphrases fit poorly, and an anti-realist's effort to preserve attitude-independent counterfactual wrongness acknowledges an important explanandum that realism accommodates directly.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The reply isolates a genuinely demanding linguistic phenomenon: ordinary judgments can represent conduct as wrong even under counterfactual changes in collective attitudes, preferences, or endorsements. Principal limitation: Acknowledging and accommodating that phenomenon concedes a shared explanandum, not the realist explanation, while the claimed inferiority of subjectivist paraphrase lacks a developed comparative linguistic standard. Live burden: The realist must show that truth-conditional, pragmatic, or standard-relative anti-realist analyses systematically mishandle relevant constructions and that realism improves explanation without disproportionate commitments. Locked score: The strong and competent band captures direct contact, clear recoverability, and important semantic pressure, while reflecting slightly overstated force, limited warrant, incomplete comparative inference, and only moderate completion of the subsidiary language burden.

con.words: Ordinary moral language gives realism no semantic priority because subjectivist or anti-realist analyses can purportedly explain the same relevant linguistic practices.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The reply squarely rejects the realist's claimed semantic priority and identifies subjectivist linguistic analysis as the appropriate location for a genuine comparative dispute. Principal limitation: The categorical denial is predominantly asserted and explicitly deferred, providing neither representative linguistic evidence nor a developed account of counterfactual, disagreement, and objectivity-marking constructions. Live burden: The anti-realist must present a specific compositional or pragmatic analysis, compare its predictions with realist semantics, and explain apparent attitude independence without simply repeating that alternative analyses exist. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects substantial responsiveness, stable core terminology, and direct relevance to the language bridge, while registering materially overstated force, weak evidential development, and insufficient engagement with the strongest comparative formulation of realist linguistic pressure.

pro.words: Historical, evolutionary, and cultural variation in moralizing concerns beliefs and practices; such contingent genealogy alone does not establish dependence or variation in mind-independent facts.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The move cleanly separates the contingent genealogy of moral belief and practice from the metaphysical status of whatever facts those beliefs purport to represent, while explicitly conceding extensive variation. Principal limitation: This distinction blocks an elementary inference but does not neutralize sophisticated genealogical challenges directed toward the reliability, justification, or truth-tracking credentials of the beliefs rather than toward facts themselves. Live burden: The realist must examine whether identified causal mechanisms systematically generate normative appearances independently of truth, and must explain what positive epistemic connection could withstand an adequately evidenced debunking account. Locked score: The very strong band reflects excellent precision, coherent qualification, and substantial defensive value, with moderated burden relevance because the move establishes a necessary distinction rather than completing the epistemological answer.

con.words: The relevant genealogical challenge concerns shared causal history and possibly unreliable philosophical training among localized realists, not the bare numerical prevalence of their view.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The reply moves beyond crude majority counting and correctly locates possible epistemic significance in shared causes, training practices, and methodological reliability among a localized group. Principal limitation: Common training may transmit expertise rather than error, and the selected evidence identifies no specific mechanism demonstrating that the shared methods are systematically unreliable or truth-insensitive. Live burden: The anti-realist must isolate an independently supported error-producing feature, distinguish sociological clustering from epistemic defeat, and show why the mechanism better explains realist convergence than competence does. Locked score: The strong and competent band recognizes coherent framing, careful possibility-level calibration, charitable contact with the belief-fact distinction, and strong responsiveness, while reflecting limited evidence and only partial completion of the subsidiary genealogical challenge.

pro.words: Genuine causal debunking explanations can undermine beliefs, but numerical prevalence cannot substitute for demonstrated unreliability because widespread views may be either true or false.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The reply grants the strongest legitimate genealogical principle while precisely distinguishing demonstrated error-producing causes from prevalence, minority status, or disagreement considered independently. Principal limitation: Establishing the correct evidential threshold does not itself vindicate realist belief or exclude future causal evidence, and the treatment of disagreement's second-order significance remains comparatively abbreviated. Live burden: The realist must evaluate the proposed mechanism on its evidence, explain any positive reliability credentials of normative appearances, and avoid treating failure of one debunking argument as affirmative realism. Locked score: The very strong band appropriately reflects outstanding charity, direct component-level responsiveness, stable distinctions, calibrated concession, and strong coherence, while recognizing that this subsidiary defense limits an objection rather than completing the broader epistemological case.

con.words: A common psychological error could explain localized realist belief while outsiders remain undecided, with population imbalance functioning only as a heuristic clue rather than the debunking mechanism.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The move precisely distinguishes ignorance from contrary belief and correctly explains how a localized error account could operate without requiring the broader population to endorse anti-realism. Principal limitation: The proposed common psychological cause remains hypothetical, and numerical localization provides only a heuristic prompt rather than independent evidence that the group's belief-forming process actually produces error. Live burden: The anti-realist must identify, measure, and substantiate the mechanism, demonstrate its relevance to realist judgment specifically, and exclude expertise or selection effects as comparably plausible explanations. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects excellent conceptual distinctions, appropriately conditional force, substantial charity, and direct responsiveness, while preserving decisive reservations about evidential warrant and the unestablished transition from possible causal explanation to genuine debunking.

pro.words: Metaethical packages should receive holistic comparison, with realism allegedly preserving substantial normative phenomena while imposing lower cumulative theoretical costs than its competitors.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: Holistic package comparison is the appropriate architecture for evaluating theories whose explanatory benefits, ontological commitments, semantic resources, and epistemological liabilities cannot sensibly be assessed in isolation. Principal limitation: The claimed realist advantage is substantially asserted rather than demonstrated, because neither plausibility points nor theoretical costs receive stable criteria or a representative accounting across developed alternatives. Live burden: The realist must itemize preserved phenomena, acknowledged commitments, and comparative liabilities for both sides, explaining why disputed anti-realist costs genuinely count without presupposing the very realist interpretation under examination. Locked score: The strong and competent band captures considerable relevance and a coherent comparative ambition, while marking materially overstated confidence, underdeveloped evidential warrant, and insufficiently specific engagement with the strongest competing packages.

con.words: Standard evolutionary and peer-disagreement objections may fail, yet realism remains allegedly superfluous because moral phenomena can be explained without its less parsimonious metaphysical posit.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The move commendably abandons conventional objections Bush considers weak and concentrates the anti-realist case upon the more promising comparative question of explanatory necessity and parsimony. Principal limitation: Superfluity is asserted more strongly than the evidence supports because descriptive explanations of behavior, belief, and discourse may not address the realist's proposed explanandum of normative truth or facts. Live burden: The anti-realist must specify a common explanandum, demonstrate that the descriptive package covers it, and justify comparing ontological costs only after explanatory adequacy has been established. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects high central relevance, commendable qualification, and coherent strategic focus, while registering limited evidential warrant, incomplete treatment of facts as data, and an underdeveloped comparative demonstration.

pro.words: Apparently intelligible metaethical questions possess prima facie legitimacy, so quietism must explain their alleged defect rather than dismiss them because answering them is difficult.
pro.critique: Strongest feature: The reply imposes a carefully defeasible burden: apparent intelligibility supplies prima facie evidence for legitimacy, while leaving open that a subsequent methodological diagnosis could overturn it. Principal limitation: Initial meaningfulness does not demonstrate metaphysical substance, and some apparently coherent questions can dissolve after semantic, pragmatic, or conceptual analysis without receiving direct answers. Live burden: The realist must preserve the modest burden formulation while clarifying what successful dissolution would require and why Bush's descriptive reorientation has not yet met that requirement. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptional charity, direct responsiveness, stable qualification, strong coherence, and decisive contact with the quietist inference, while appropriately stopping short of treating prima facie legitimacy as a completed defense of realism.

con.words: A pragmatist program explains moral behavior, psychology, and language descriptively while rejecting standard metaethical problem-setting, leaving no apparent problem for realism to solve.
con.critique: Strongest feature: The move presents a recognizably distinct methodological program informed by ordinary-language inquiry, experimental philosophy, and cognitive science rather than merely negating realist metaphysics. Principal limitation: Describing moral behavior, psychology, and discourse does not automatically dissolve questions about normative truth, while pragmatism, quietism, and the relevant criterion of dissolution remain only partially operationalized. Live burden: The anti-realist must explain why apparently intelligible truth questions are defective or idle, show how the descriptive framework handles their practical function, and compare rather than bypass the realist explanandum. Locked score: The strong and competent band recognizes substantial central relevance, useful methodological breadth, and explicit perspective-level qualification, while preserving significant reservations about conceptual precision, evidential development, and engagement with the strongest irreducible-truth formulation.

strengths: Clearly defined robust realism and connected mind-independent normative truth directly to the debate's central motion.
Distinguished the genealogy of beliefs and practices from the metaphysical status of facts while expressly conceding historical and cultural variation.
Answered epistemic symmetry by separating inability to compel assent from defeat of justification or automatic parity.
Granted that genuine causal debunking matters, then precisely challenged prevalence and disagreement as substitutes for an evidenced mechanism.
Placed a fair defeasible burden upon quietist dissolution by acknowledging that later evidence could overturn apparent intelligibility.

blunders.text: The claimed lower-cost holistic advantage remained insufficiently itemized across developed rival packages and shared comparative criteria.
The counterfactual-language reply moved too quickly from a shared explanandum to an alleged concession favoring the realist explanation.

strengths: Accepted the broadened normative scope and clearly preserved global opposition without exploiting an artificial moral versus nonmoral boundary.
Challenged inherited anti-realist cost assignments while retaining the legitimacy of holistic comparison as a common method.
Separated serious first-order moral opposition from substantive metaethical commitment and avoided attributing implicit anti-realism to ordinary speakers.
Refined genealogy into a causal reliability question rather than relying upon majority opinion or raw population imbalance.
Conceded weaknesses in familiar evolutionary and disagreement objections, concentrating instead upon parsimony and explanatory necessity.

blunders.text: The categorical denial of realist linguistic priority was largely deferred and lacked a developed comparative semantic analysis.
The proposed localized psychological error remained hypothetical, without independent evidence identifying an unreliable common mechanism.
The pragmatist dissolution described moral practice but did not yet show that questions about normative truth were defective or explanatorily idle.

finalArgument.thesis: The strongest realist case treats objective normative facts as the best component of a holistic explanation of deliberative authority, counterfactual stability, and justified normative correction.
premises: Deliberation presents some considerations as reasons whose authority is not exhausted by an agent's present desires, endorsements, or social conventions.
Counterfactual moral judgments remain intelligible when speakers imagine altered collective attitudes, suggesting that attitude variation and correctness conditions perform distinguishable roles.
A genealogy defeats normative belief only when evidence connects its causal mechanism to unreliability; cultural variation or localized membership alone cannot supply that connection.
A fair comparison should count realism's ontology against any semantic, psychological, and pragmatic machinery rivals require to preserve deliberation, disagreement, and correction.
finalArgument.conclusion: If realism explains these phenomena more comprehensively under symmetric cost accounting, objective normative facts are provisionally warranted despite continuing epistemological and ontological objections.

newArguments.title: Normative error without endorsement
newArguments.text: Practices of moral correction distinguish changing someone's attitudes from showing those attitudes mistaken. A purely attitude-dependent account can reproduce the social act of correction, but it must explain why participants regard improved information and consistency as revealing error rather than merely producing new preferences. Realism offers a direct interpretation: correction aims, however imperfectly, at reasons that are not constituted by the corrected person's former endorsement. This does not prove realism, but it adds a specific phenomenon to the holistic comparison.

newArguments.title: Symmetric theoretical accounting
newArguments.text: Ontological parsimony should not be evaluated independently of explanatory complexity. An anti-realist theory may posit fewer kinds of facts yet require elaborate semantic, pragmatic, and psychological resources to explain disagreement, counterfactual stability, and deliberative authority. Conversely, realism must count its epistemology and metaphysics openly. A theory-by-theory ledger comparing common phenomena, auxiliary commitments, and residual problems would convert the transcript's informal plausibility points into a transparent method and prevent either side from receiving cost-free explanatory machinery.

finalArgument.thesis: The strongest anti-realist case holds that objective normative facts are unwarranted unless they add explanatory power beyond empirically grounded accounts of moral psychology, language, and social regulation.
premises: Ordinary speakers can condemn conduct, deliberate seriously, and express counterfactual commitments without possessing any determinate implicit theory about mind-independent normative facts.

Meaning-in-use accounts can analyze moral assertions through standards, commitments, communicative intentions, and inferential practices while preserving sincere disagreement as a practical phenomenon.
Causal explanations of normative belief become epistemically relevant only when a demonstrated mechanism predicts error or insensitivity, not merely because believers form a minority.
If descriptive accounts explain behavior, discourse, deliberation, and correction without objective facts, realism must identify an additional phenomenon that its posit explains distinctively.
finalArgument.conclusion: Absent a demonstrated explanatory remainder uniquely favoring objective normative facts, global normative anti-realism remains a proportionate interpretation of moral and epistemic practice.

newArguments.title: Intervention-based explanatory test
newArguments.text: Competing metaethical explanations can be compared through intervention. If changes in information, incentives, identity, social coordination, or emotional salience systematically predict changes in moral judgment, descriptive mechanisms gain explanatory support. Realism may still interpret some resulting judgments as more accurate, but it should identify additional predictions or explanatory constraints contributed by objective facts. This test does not assume that causal explanation settles truth; it asks whether the realist posit produces identifiable explanatory value beyond the psychological and social model.

newArguments.title: Metaethical underdetermination of practice
newArguments.text: The same stable practice can support multiple metaethical interpretations. Speakers may condemn cruelty across counterfactual changes because their evaluative standards are deeply entrenched, because discourse conventionally suppresses perspective parameters, or because they track mind-independent reasons. If these interpretations predict the same ordinary behavior and language, practice alone underdetermines metaphysics. The realist must identify discriminating evidence, while the anti-realist must provide an explicit semantic model. This mutual demand strengthens anti-realism by denying default priority without pretending that compatibility already establishes explanatory equality.
